title: apply a reviewed project command from an authenticated terminal
input: The operator chooses the intended project and the approved resource command.
action: Cloud Shell supplies an authenticated command environment with supported cloud tools. The selected CLI invokes the resource APIs under configured credentials; the shell itself is not the production application runtime.
output: The operator inspects the API result and confirms the intended resource state.
check: Verify account, project, permissions and actual changed resource before closing the operational request.

title: preserve an existing source repository in a supported development workflow
input: The maintainer inventories repository history, branch controls and dependent build triggers.
action: Cloud Source Repositories hosts existing supported Git repositories within its service lifecycle and availability constraints. Migration preserves commits and access controls and redirects build triggers to the chosen supported source platform.
output: The build pipeline checks out the accepted revision from the replacement repository and produces the normal artifact.
check: Compare commit history, branch permissions, trigger authentication and reproducible builds before switching source references.

title: train a model with supported TPU workers
input: The ML engineer selects the framework, supported TPU topology and authorized training dataset.
action: Cloud TPU supplies configured tensor-accelerator capacity for supported model execution. Training code partitions computation using the chosen framework; input-pipeline throughput and checkpoints govern the complete training job.
output: The training application persists accepted checkpoints and evaluates the resulting model.
check: Test supported operators, topology, checkpoint restart and real accelerator utilization before expanding the training run.

title: provide a restricted cloud development environment
input: The developer requests a permitted workstation configuration for the assigned project.
action: Cloud Workstations provisions the configured development environment and access endpoint. Development tools run in that environment; repository access, runtime credentials and network restrictions remain explicitly configured.
output: The developer builds the project and commits accepted code to the authorized repository.
check: Test workstation access, dependency network paths, persistent workspace data and removal of developer assignment.

title: coordinate an AI compute cluster's deployment and operations
input: The platform owner selects the supported cluster configuration, compute resources and AI workload requirements.
action: Cluster Director provisions compute, network and storage for the selected AI or HPC cluster and supplies managed Slurm job scheduling. Slurm assigns the training tasks to available workers; topology-aware placement and worker recovery support the configured cluster lifecycle.
output: The owner schedules the accepted AI workload only after its cluster resources and network dependencies are ready.
check: Check current supported architecture, resource health, topology and recovery before running the production training job.

title: deploy an HPC environment from a reviewed blueprint
input: The HPC owner selects a supported toolkit blueprint, compute sizes and shared-storage configuration.
action: Cluster Toolkit generates or coordinates supported infrastructure deployment from the configured blueprint and modules. The deployed scheduler and workers run the scientific jobs; the toolkit is deployment tooling rather than a solver.
output: The scientist submits a sample job to the created cluster and validates the shared dataset path.
check: Review the generated plan, permissions, job execution and complete resource cleanup before accepting the blueprint.

title: run an authorized analytical notebook with a managed runtime
input: The analyst opens a reviewed notebook and selects its permitted dataset and runtime configuration.
action: Colab Enterprise supplies the configured notebook execution runtime and project integration. Notebook code performs the analysis under its runtime service account; notebook sharing does not bypass dataset permissions.
output: The analyst persists accepted code and analytical outputs in the approved project locations.
check: Test runtime identity, shared-notebook access, reproducibility and cleanup of sensitive temporary output.

title: provision a cloud resource through a Kubernetes resource definition
input: The platform maintainer submits an approved Kubernetes custom resource for the selected cloud service.
action: Config Connector reconciles supported custom resource definitions with corresponding Google Cloud resources using its configured identity. The controller applies resource state; workload pods use the created resource separately.
output: The application binds to the created resource after the controller reports the accepted state.
check: Test controller permissions, reconcile failures, deletion policy and actual cloud resource readiness before deployment.

title: apply reviewed cloud configuration through a managed controller environment
input: The platform owner supplies supported resource definitions and approved controller access.
action: Config Controller hosts supported configuration-management controllers for declarative cloud resource administration. The configured reconciliation components apply desired resource state; application services execute the business workload.
output: The owner validates the created resources and their effective policies before exposing the application.
check: Check resource ownership, reconciliation status, deletion behavior and the controller's scoped cloud permissions.

title: synchronize approved Kubernetes configuration from a trusted source
input: The platform maintainer commits reviewed cluster or namespace configuration to the configured source.
action: Config Sync reconciles supported Kubernetes objects from the approved source into selected clusters. It applies declared configuration; deployment controllers and pods handle runtime rollout and application execution.
output: The owner checks applied objects and workload readiness before accepting the configuration release.
check: Test invalid configuration, source authentication, ownership conflicts and rollback to the accepted revision.
